pathogen.value: Eimeria species protozoa (e.g. E. tenella, E. necatrix, E. acervulina, E. brunetti, E. maxima, E. mitis, E. praecox affect chickens)

value: ingesting contaminated feed, water, litter or soil
spread by equipment, footwear, insects and rodents
can be fatal especially in young or sick birds

mortality.value: varies from none in mild cases to high mortality in severe outbreaks, especially in young birds

incubation_period.value: disease develops rapidly, over about 4 to 7 days from ingestion of infective oocysts

diagnosis.value: finding oocysts in a fecal sample under a microscope, along with checking for characteristic gut damage at necropsy

value: keeping birds off damp litter and away from droppings
raising birds on wire floors reduces exposure

treatment_overview.value: anticoccidial medication given in water once signs appear, along with supportive care to manage dehydration and prevent secondary bacterial infection

when_to_call_vet.value: Call a vet if chicks or young birds develop bloody or watery diarrhea with lethargy and poor appetite, since coccidiosis can turn fatal quickly.

summary.value: Coccidiosis is a common intestinal parasite disease of young chickens, spread through droppings that contaminate feed, water and litter. It causes diarrhea and poor growth and can kill quickly if untreated, but it is well controlled with anticoccidial feed additives or chick vaccination.
